rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: Blackout: Oct hold 84-87%; Dec hike ~89.5% (Oct-15 vintage); BoC Oct odds 25-32%
rows.read: The Fed stays silent — blackout Oct 17-29, October priced as a hold at ~84-87%, December the debate (~89.5% hike, Oct-15 vintage — stale, flag). The ECB holds Oct 29 (70/73 economists), December the live meeting (64/73). The BoC's October-28 hike option sits at just 25-32% after the -68.3K jobs miss — Canada CPI today 7:30am CT is the settler. BoE Nov 5 is ~95% priced (UK CPI Wed fc 3.4%). RBNZ Oct 28 two-way (NZ CPI Wed). BoJ Oct 29-30: Oct-30 hike ~25%, December ~80% (OIS). RBA Nov 2-3: Kent questions whether 4.60% is 'restrictive enough' — ~30% priced, December ~50%.

US: IP +0.7% beat vs NY Fed services -20.7 warning. Today: Canada CPI 7:30am CT + BoC business survey 10:30am CT. This week: PBoC LPR Tue (hold expected), US housing Tue, UK labor Tue, UK CPI Wed, NZ CPI Wed, Japan CPI Fri, flash PMIs Fri.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: No retaliation yet, talks stalled — haven bid sheathed at Monday's open; France unrest hits the euro
rows.read: Sunday's two fears both fizzled at the open: no signed Iran deal (talks stalled; sequencing deadlock) and no Hezbollah retaliation (decision pending; IDF: normal routines) — the haven bid stayed sheathed, DXY flat 101.80-101.83. The Hormuz mine claim is still unconfirmed (no ship names, no verification). The weekend's real market move is in France: violent cost-of-living protests, Macron's Sunday address, OAT-Bund ~140bp — the euro's first domestic headwind in days. The Graham waiver stands amid bipartisan backlash, no reversal.

GDT dairy Tuesday is the next terms-of-trade pulse.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.figure: FY26 $1.992T; Graham waiver stands (backlash, no reversal); France: vote Tue, Moody's Fri
rows.read: The books stand: FY2026 deficit $1.992T — largest in five years (~6.2% of GDP); tariff refunds ($145B) ate record customs duties, debt service hit a record $1.36T. The Graham Act waiver stands — armed, unfired — amid bipartisan backlash but no reversal signal. France: revenue-section vote Tue Oct 20, Moody's review Fri Oct 23; OAT-Bund ~140bp after the unrest — the euro's fiscal channel is the week to watch.
